hypothesis: Published evidence of a weekend anomaly in gold may transfer to physically backed European gold ETCs after executable timing and current LSE costs.

evidence_context.support: Borowski and Lukasik report a weekend effect in gold while finding no general monthly or weekday effect.
evidence_context.caution: Calendar effects are market- and period-dependent; this is a falsification test, not an assumption that the anomaly survives.

calendar_policy: Require an observed Friday followed by an observed Monday exactly three calendar days later; skip holidays rather than relabel adjacent sessions.
position: long only, no leverage, one independent round trip per eligible weekend
cost_basis: Current IBKR UK minima approximated as GBP1/order tiered and GBP3/order fixed; stress adds 10 bps round-trip. Percentage diagnostics avoid mixing GBp/GBP/USD listing quote units.

gates.maximum_cross_listing_return_correlation: report only; dates need not align because LSE holidays should align mostly

multiple_testing: All three variants are reported. A candidate exists only if the exact same variant independently passes every frozen gate on both listings; no post-result variants or threshold changes.
